solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: In New York, rough country smell over harbour areas (9)

blocks.note: on = over, about (a book on birds)
docks are the working areas of a harbour

annotation.surface: A visitor to New York wrinkles their nose at the rank smell drifting over from the waterfront.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In New York' reads as the scene of the smell, but it only marks the definition as American usage.
annotation.definitionFit: The boondocks is American slang for remote, rough backcountry.

entries.clue: Curving coastline of great height (5)

blocks.note: HT is the standard abbreviation for height

annotation.surface: A description of a stretch of coast with towering cliffs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Great height' reads as one phrase about tall cliffs, but it splits into two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A bight is a long, gentle curve in a coastline, like the Great Australian Bight.

entries.clue: Old broken fire door unserviceable, causing a stink (11)

indicatorNotes.broken: something broken has its parts out of order

blocks.note: U/S = unserviceable, British forces shorthand for out of action

annotation.surface: A complaint about a smelly old fire door in a run-down building.
annotation.walkthrough: U/S for 'unserviceable' (useless, broken) is British slang that crosswords use often.
annotation.definitionFit: Odoriferous means giving off a smell, usually an unpleasant one.

entries.clue: Upmarket shop — note, one cutting locks (7)

blocks.note: lah is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A notice about a smart shop where one member of staff cuts hair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Locks' looks like security hardware or a hairdresser's work; it is Samson's hair, which Delilah had cut to steal his strength.
annotation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Delilah betrayed Samson by having his hair cut off.

entries.clue: By which one may see cowboy party shoot (8)

annotation.definition: By which one may see cowboy

blocks.note: a camp is a party or faction

annotation.surface: A cowboy spotted at a party where someone starts shooting.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint: cowboys gathered round a campfire at night, lit by its glow.
annotation.definitionFit: A campfire is the light by which you would see a cowboy on the trail at night.

entries.clue: Self-important, never entering dirty home (6)

indicatorNotes.entering: one word entering another goes inside it, so NOT goes into STY

blocks.note: not = never, in the sense 'not at all'
a sty is a pig's filthy pen

annotation.surface: A snob who would never set foot in a messy house.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is itself a snotty attitude, which helps the definition hide in plain view.
annotation.definitionFit: Snotty means snooty, full of one's own importance.

entries.clue: Marsh was awash with plants initially (5)

annotation.definition: Marsh was awash with plants initially

indicatorNotes.awash: a word awash is sloshed about
indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letters of Marsh and plants

annotation.surface: A wetland description: water everywhere and vegetation taking hold.
annotation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes a swamp, so every word does double duty.
annotation.definitionFit: A swamp is a marsh flooded with water and thick with plants.

entries.clue: An excess of what we do to internet with electronic input (7)

indicatorNotes.input: an input is something put in, so E is put into SURF IT

annotation.surface: A grumble about how much of our time goes into browsing online.
annotation.walkthrough: 'What we do to internet' is a two-word phrase, verb plus pronoun: we surf it.
annotation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excessive amount of something.

entries.clue: Predatory flyer returned driving off small seabird (3)

indicatorNotes.returned: something returned goes back the way it came, so SKUA is read backwards
indicatorNotes.driving off: to drive off is to chase away, so the S is chased out of AUKS

blocks.note: the skua is a seabird that attacks other birds

annotation.surface: A bird of prey circles back and chases off a little seabird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small seabird' reads as one phrase, but 'small' is the S to be removed and 'seabird' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The auk is a seabird of the North Atlantic, the puffin's family.

entries.clue: Match right pen when it’s woven paper (9)

indicatorNotes.when it’s woven: the letters are woven together into a new order

annotation.surface: Picking a pen to go with woven paper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a verb meaning 'pair up', but it is just letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Parchment is a stiff writing material, and also a type of heavy paper.

entries.clue: Gross member of parliament’s grumble (5)

blocks.note: a group of owls is called a parliament

annotation.surface: A disgusting politician moans about something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Member of parliament' wants to be MP; here the parliament is a flock of owls.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to growl and to grumble are both to complain in a low, surly voice.

entries.clue: Spooner’s spelling individual Wiltshire resident (9)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: Rev Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: a rune maker writes magic spells; swap R and M

annotation.surface: An odd pairing of a champion speller with a West Country local.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spelling' means casting spells, not writing words correctly. Moonrakers are Wiltshire folk, after smugglers who said they were raking a pond for the moon's reflection.
annotation.definitionFit: Moonraker is a traditional nickname for someone from Wiltshire, an English county.

entries.clue: Errant lost fight badly — such a contest? (5,2,8)

indicatorNotes.badly: the letters are placed badly, out of order

annotation.surface: A wandering knight is beaten in combat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Such a contest' points back to the fight in the surface: a fight is a trial of strength.
annotation.definitionFit: A trial of strength is a contest deciding who is stronger.

entries.clue: Stomach light tea which is a bit rubbery (5-6)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a descriptive phrase; the answer is the noun it describes

blocks.note: a taper is a thin candle
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

annotation.surface: Someone who can only stomach weak tea finds a snack chewy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Light tea' reads as a weak brew or small meal; the words split into a candle and a cuppa.
annotation.definitionFit: Gutta-percha is a tough latex from Malaysian trees, rubber-like but harder.

entries.clue: What has each one represented for area in sector? (3,5)

annotation.definition: What has each one represented for area in sector?

blocks.note: the surface pushes an MP standing for a constituency; the setter means each value drawn to scale as an area
not a business sector but a slice of a circle, the wedge a value occupies

annotation.surface: A question about regional representation, as in which area each member stands for.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Represented', 'area' and 'sector' sound like politics or business; in a pie chart each value is shown by the area of its sector.
annotation.definitionFit: A pie chart shows each quantity as a sector whose area is proportional to it.

entries.clue: Love twin avoiding you following dad’s dance (4,5)

indicatorNotes.avoiding: to avoid something is to keep clear of it, so DOUBLE keeps clear of U
indicatorNotes.following: following means coming after, so O and DOBLE come after PA'S

blocks.note: O = love, a zero score in tennis
a double is a twin, a lookalike
U sounds like you, as in text speak; removed

annotation.surface: A twin sneaking away from someone while copying their father's moves.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces are assembled out of clue order: 'following' puts PA'S first.
annotation.definitionFit: The paso doble is a Latin ballroom dance modelled on a bullfight.

entries.clue: Figure to take action about tasteless articles (6)

indicatorNotes.about: about means surrounding, so SUE goes around TAT

blocks.note: to sue is to take legal action

annotation.surface: Someone ready to go to court over a load of tacky goods.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take action' looks like 'do something'; it is legal action.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a figure in sculpture is a statue.

entries.clue: Insufficiently deal with good loser? (8)

annotation.surface: A complaint about someone who fails to handle a gracious loser properly.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that an underdog is only the expected loser, and may well win.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the underdog is the side everyone expects to lose, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Slump ends in markets’ fall that hurts (6)

indicatorNotes.ends in: take the last letters of markets and fall

blocks.note: ouch! is what you say when something hurts

annotation.surface: A financial report on a painful market crash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slump' and 'fall' both look like the market news; 'Slump' is the posture and 'fall' only gives its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: To slump is to slouch, sitting or standing with drooping shoulders.

entries.clue: What’s wet and clammy? (7)

blocks.note: the surface pushes damp weather or skin; the setter means a liquid dish, a soup
not cold and sweaty but full of clams, the shellfish

annotation.surface: A riddle about something damp and sticky.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clammy' means damp and cold, but here it means full of clams: clam chowder is a soup.
annotation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick soup, famously made with clams.

entries.clue: What could be inspired, composed à la Ninth (8)

indicatorNotes.composed: the letters are composed into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A piece of music written in the style of Beethoven's Ninth, inspired by it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inspired' and 'composed' both look musical; 'inspired' literally means breathed in.
annotation.definitionFit: An inhalant is a medicine or vapour taken in by breathing.

entries.clue: Approach after knowing point of entry? (7)

indicatorNotes.after: after means coming later in order, so WAY comes after ARCH

blocks.note: arch = knowing, sly, as in an arch look
a way is an approach, a route or method

annotation.surface: Advice to go in only once you know where the entrance is.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: an archway rises to a point.
annotation.definitionFit: An archway is an entrance under an arch, often a pointed one.

entries.clue: Rework article penned by gun representative (6)

indicatorNotes.penned by: penned means shut in a pen, so A is enclosed by REV and MP

blocks.note: to gun an engine is to rev it
an MP is an elected representative in Parliament

annotation.surface: A gun lobbyist writing an article that needs redrafting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gun' looks like a firearm; here it is a verb, to rev an engine hard.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to revamp a piece of work is to redo it in improved form.

entries.clue: Perhaps mate found way of paying for Georgia (10,5)

blocks.note: check is the American spelling of cheque

annotation.surface: Someone's partner turns up a way of settling a bill for a woman called Georgia.
annotation.walkthrough: Georgia is the US state, marking the American spelling. 'Mate' is checkmate: a discovered check, where moving one piece unmasks another's attack, can deliver it.
annotation.definitionFit: A discovered check in chess may also be mate, so mate is an example of it.

entries.clue: Craft getting an ox to follow back of truck (5)

indicatorNotes.back of: the back of a word is its last letter
indicatorNotes.to follow: to follow is to come behind, so A YAK comes behind K

blocks.note: a yak is a Himalayan ox

annotation.surface: An ox trudging behind a truck.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a skill; here it is a boat.
annotation.definitionFit: A kayak is a small paddled boat, and craft means a vessel.

entries.clue: Fast means of sending vegetable, saving energy by day (9)

indicatorNotes.saving: saving means except: E is left out
indicatorNotes.by: D is placed by (next to) the rest

annotation.surface: Rushing fresh vegetables by express post while cutting fuel use each day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saving energy' reads as being green; 'saving' means except, so the E goes.
annotation.definitionFit: Broadband is a high-speed internet connection, a fast way of sending data.

entries.clue: Ancient keep, the first to be destroyed (3)

indicatorNotes.the first to be destroyed: the first letter of HOLD is knocked out

annotation.surface: A ruined castle: the old keep was the first part to fall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a castle tower, which suits the surface; it is the verb, to hold.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though ancient usually means very old indeed.

entries.clue: Loopy route — around 100 kilometres (5)

indicatorNotes.around: around means encircling, so WAY encircles C and K

annotation.surface: A winding road about a hundred kilometres long.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loopy' looks like a description of the winding route, but it is the definition: crazy.
annotation.definitionFit: Loopy and wacky both mean crazy or eccentric.

entries.clue: Joiner dismissing wide tree (5)

indicatorNotes.dismissing: W is sent away from WELDER

blocks.note: W = wide, a cricket extra; removed

annotation.surface: A carpenter getting rid of an overly broad tree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' wants to be a carpenter; the joiner here works in metal. In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach.
annotation.definitionFit: The elder is a small tree with white flowers and dark berries.

entries.clue: Carry moneybox containing cents, not note (9)

indicatorNotes.containing: C is held inside the word
indicatorNotes.not: N is taken out to make room

annotation.surface: Taking your piggy bank along, full of coins and no banknotes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a banknote, which fits the surface; it is just N.
annotation.definitionFit: To piggyback someone is to carry them on your back.
